result:
All 59 tests pass, including the new regression test.

Applied the upstream Jinja2 fix (pallets/jinja@66587ce) for this bug in `src/jinja2/idtracking.py`:

- `Symbols.branch_update` previously skipped fixing up a variable's load if it was stored in *every* branch of an if/elif/else (`if branch_count == len(branch_symbols): continue`). That "all branches set it" check was based on a flawed per-target loop that also incorrectly `continue`d early whenever a target happened to already be in `self.stores`, which masked cases where the variable still needed to fall back to a resolve/alias load â€” causing it to end up `undefined`.
- Replaced the counting logic with a simpler set-difference (`stores.difference_update(self.stores)`) and removed the `branch_count == len(branch_symbols)` skip entirely, so the parameter is always re-loaded correctly regardless of how many branches set it.

Also added the upstream regression test (`test_load_parameter_when_set_in_all_if_branches` in `tests/test_regression.py`) and the CHANGES.rst entry (`:issue:1253`).
